definition: Mean TEST accuracy (%) over the five registered terminal epochs; training uses the same window. 100→95..99, 250→245..249, 772→767..771, ImageNet489g1 common80→75..79, ImageNet489g2 84→79..83. Accuracy differences and across-seed SD/SE use percentage points (pp).
CSV plateau means last20epochs, not the primary. Final and best are distinct secondary metrics.

Sample standard deviation (ddof1) and standard error SD/sqrt(n) across raw per-seed plateau5 values, never estimated from a printed mean. Singletons have SD/SE=null. Historical scorer bars can use pooled/prior sigma and are not these descriptive arm error bars.
Epoch accuracy lines are printed to0.01 percentage point; derived five-epoch averages inherit that precision.
Comparisons stay within batch unless explicitly labeled descriptive across batches.
(arm mean minus in-batch scalar mean)/(in-batch layerwise mean minus scalar mean); endpoints0and1 are constructed, not discoveries.
Mean test accuracy over the final five completed epochs, in percent. Differences use percentage points.
Mean over the last 20 epochs. At a 20-epoch budget it is the whole-run mean, a speed/AUC proxy. Preserve only in historical correction tables.
1/[1+(m-1)rho_s], a dimensionless effective-independence fraction for the measured sign statistic under an exchangeable-variance approximation. It is not percent signal or a performance predictor.
Excess temporal variance of the pooled negative-sign fraction over an independence floor, normalized by Bernoulli variance. Name whether the floor is pooled or heterogeneity-corrected.
An implied per-weight correlation derived from the rung measurement at average group size k. It is distinct from the marginal-sign statistic E.

100*(R_corrected(u)-mean R_null(u)), where R=SS_block|tensor/(SS_block|tensor+SS_within) after noise correction, applied to persistent per-coordinate negative-sign frequency. Units: percentage points of explained variance, not accuracy.
Block size in output-channel row units: max(1,round(row_width*u)) coordinates per convolution-tensor block. u=1 is an output channel; u=1/512 spans 1–9 coordinates across these tensors.
Monte Carlo SE of a within-tensor permutation-null mean using three random null draws. This is not training-seed SEM.
The c55 steady-half time average of max(beta)-min(beta), then averaged across layerwise, nodewise and weightwise. Natural-log units. Terminal weightwise span is a different summary.
Observed output-channel by input-channel interaction sum of squares divided by the corresponding within-tensor permutation-null sum of squares. Dimensionless; registered threshold 1.10.

Disagree / determinate 100-meta-step windows from virtual regrouping of the cru1 layerwise trajectory. Pooled denominator weighting differs from the mean of per-seed rates. Do not substitute the 12-epoch true-m2 per-step fraction.
L_i = 0.9*m_i + 0.1*z_i. Positive L lowers beta (log step size), negative L raises beta. Statistics of seed means and statistics of probe records are separate.
Three-carrier signed sum exceeds the sum of absolute remaining terms. Distinct from removal flipping the aggregate sign; the latter holds on all pinned records, the former does not.
Documented fitted tau (epochs) and normalized hitting times rho25, rho50, rho75, rho90. Tau SD is across three training seeds; no SE or rho uncertainty is reconstructed.
Blank means unavailable or inapplicable, never zero. SD/SE are copied only when provided; no SD/SE is inferred from rounded means, t values, ranges, or records treated as seeds.

Floating values are copied to 15 significant digits to suppress binary representation tails. Printed historical values keep their supplied numerical precision. This is serialization only, not a new estimate.
